chosen.chosen: The answer recommends one option for each of the three questions (POSIX sh; ln -P then rm -f with a check first; GitHub Actions on ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-26.04 and macos-latest) instead of only laying the options side by side.
chosen.why: The research's receiver builds docs/architecture.md on it and the user approves that; an answer they can take as said keeps each reader from drawing their own, while the tables still show every option weighed.

chosen.chosen: ubuntu-26.04 is named as a third test runner beside ubuntu-24.04 and macos-latest.
chosen.why: Ubuntu has shipped the Rust coreutils as its core utilities since 25.10, so ubuntu-latest (24.04, GNU) alone would not test the ln and rm a current Ubuntu user runs; that the 26.04 runner's ln is the Rust one is left in Not settled.

chosen.chosen: Sources are cited as [S1]..[S21] in the text with one list at the end, each with its URL, version or date, and line numbers for source code and NEWS.
chosen.why: Each source is written once and pointed to from every fact that rests on it, so a reader opens it from one place and the text stays short.

chosen.chosen: The name order of the list (locale-dependent glob order) and the wording of ln's error for cannot move: REASON are written as Not settled, for the architecture or a test to settle, rather than asked of the user now.
chosen.why: They bear on how the tool is built, which the architecture stage decides; the research names what would settle each and flags that the order is the user's point only if it changes what they see.
